motion.name: camera-entry
motion.purpose: Runtime perspective moves from the chair and slumped person into the player's eyes; the transition begins after the opening hold.

motion.name: nuclear-burst
motion.purpose: The distant fireball begins, then develops into a lobed mushroom cap, stem, dust, spatial debris and an expanding ground shock ring.

motion.name: choice-start
motion.purpose: Movement, stance, facing, mouse look, drag look, nearby coffee and shelter-door interaction become available while alive and unpaused.

motion.name: runtime-render
motion.value: requestAnimationFrame; 65ms desktop / 85ms compact paint interval; dt <= 0.08s
motion.purpose: Generate the current 3D world into one ASCII pre from player and explosion state.

motion.name: coffee-sip
motion.purpose: Move the sampled first-person hand and cup while nearby; enforce action availability through the native disabled state.

motion.name: death-reset
motion.purpose: Only death freezes player choices, lowers the camera and automatically begins another round. Survivors retain their view and choose when to restart.

motion.name: reduced-motion-start
motion.purpose: Keep the opening chair and person still until explicit start, including after restart and the next round.

motion.name: lifecycle
motion.value: hidden: stop time; visible blur: pause; release capture and clear independent inputs
motion.purpose: Pause, blur, hidden state, restart, death and pointer-lock changes release or clear mouse, drag and held movement state without catch-up jumps.

motion.name: walkable-shelter
motion.purpose: Descend behind the chair, open the door and walk into x ±2.6 / z -5.05..-9.6. Camera height follows the floor; analytical room rays fill wall, floor, ceiling and closed-door depth.

motion.name: shelter-door
motion.value: angle 0 to π/2; crossing at >= 1.3 radians
motion.purpose: E prioritizes the nearby door. Rotate its points and normals around the left hinge; passage requires an open target and centered player.

motion.name: shelter-protection
motion.value: in room; closed target; angle <= 0.04 radians
motion.purpose: Survive the arriving shockwave only inside with the door fully closed. A closed door while outside or an open door while inside leaves the player unprotected.

motion.name: aftermath
motion.purpose: Allow opening the door and walking back to terrain craters and ruins without moving the camera automatically. R remains a voluntary restart.

motion.name: relative-mouse-look
motion.value: pointer lock; pitch ±1.28 radians; drag fallback
motion.purpose: Mouse clicking requests capture; rightward relative movement increases yaw. Esc, pause, blur, visibility, reset and death release capture and invalidate pending requests. A late cancelled grant exits even after resume. Direct look cancels B/F turn targets.

motion.name: independent-touch-input
motion.value: keyboard set + pointer map + activation pulses
motion.purpose: Hold movement and run with independent fingers while dragging the view; release or cancellation removes only its owning pointer.

components.name: Stance action
components.description: Native rise/sit target away from the shelter door; E prioritizes opening or closing the nearby door. Returning to the seat requires chair proximity.

components.name: Unavailable coffee
components.description: Native disabled appearance when choice time, proximity, cooldown or life state prevents a sip.

components.name: Shelter door action
components.description: Enabled near the underground door; open it to walk in or out, then close it fully from inside before the shockwave. The runtime switches the opening/closing label.

components.name: Pause and resume
components.description: The same visual button displays 暂停 or 继续 as scene time pauses or resumes; this snippet records appearance only.

components.name: Reduced-motion start
components.description: Explicit start is shown while reduced motion keeps the opening scene at time zero.

components.name: Touch movement
components.description: Compact hold targets support independent movement and run fingers alongside drag look. Releasing one pointer preserves other input. The run target shows held appearance; no runtime is included in this snippet.

components.name: Plain author label
components.description: Unclickable attribution text in the desktop footer, hidden in compact layouts; it does not navigate.

components.name: Live scene status
components.description: A polite live region reserves a line of quiet narrative and action feedback beneath the world.

narrative.overview:
This is the built visual system for the personal site at `/@lightjunction/web/`, an Experience surface. A chair and a slumped person become the visitor's body inside a real-time 3D ASCII nuclear scene, with a walkable underground shelter behind the chair. The user fixed the subject, rendering language, first-person choices and closed-door route to survival; the work owns the viewport and the interface stays quiet. [SURFACE.md](SURFACE.md) preserves that direction.

A charcoal stage, gray-white glyphs and a sparse perspective floor give the world its space. The opening side three-quarter view separates the brighter slumped person from the quieter chair, then moves into the seated person's eyes. Chinese status text and native text buttons sit below the world. This personal artwork has its own visual identity, separate from the bright `/@root/web/` introduction.
keyCharacteristics: Runtime three-dimensional surface sampling, perspective, depth and character-density shading.
A single adaptive ASCII world: 112 by 60 cells on desktop, 76 by 56 below 600px.
Third person enters first person over six seconds; a distant nuclear burst appears at eight seconds and choices open at 8.5 seconds.
Movement, facing, stance, coffee and a walkable shelter change the outcome; survival requires being inside with the door fully closed.
Survivors can leave into cratered ground and ruins at scene time 28 seconds; only death automatically begins another round after six seconds.
Native buttons, keyboard, relative mouse look and independent multitouch input with explicit reduced-motion start and lifecycle pauses.
One self-contained HTML file with one hash-pinned inline runtime and no external assets or requests.
dos: **Do** preserve the user-fixed chair, slumped person, first-person choices and walkable closed-door shelter route to survival.
**Do** keep aftermath exploration under the survivor's control and reserve automatic restart for death.
**Do** generate the 7-bit ASCII world from current three-dimensional state with perspective, depth and lighting.
**Do** require an explicit start under reduced motion, including after reset and the next round.
**Do** preserve native disabled states, visible focus, independent multitouch input, capture release and explicit pause on visible-page blur.
**Do** publish only the final `index.html` and pin its sole inline script by the exact build hash in an opaque sandbox.
donts: **Don't** import the separate `/@root/web/` brand into this personal artwork.
**Don't** substitute prerecorded playback for the interactive world or add WebGL, external fonts, image assets, audio or external requests.
**Don't** add navigation or forms, or grant same-origin access, wildcard scripts or unpinned inline-script execution for this scene.
**Don't** replace walking into the shelter with teleportation, grant protection to a player outside its closed door, or let movement, door, stance, facing or coffee act after death.
**Don't** retain held input or mouse capture across pause, blur, hidden state, restart or death.
**Don't** treat documented test coverage or local evidence as proof of final review or public signed publication.
